source.original_text: The actual Gaussian on the midpoint cosine spectrum has the following two exact means. Both integrands are integrable. M=\mathbb E\|U\|^2=\frac d{\sqrt\kappa}\frac{1-r^{2d}}{1+r^{2d}},\qquad(-1)^n\mu_n=(-1)^n\mathbb E[U^\top D_nU]=\frac d{\sqrt\kappa}\frac{r^n-r^{2d-n}}{1+r^{2d}}. Fix \(d\in\mathbb N\), \(d\ge2\), \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\), \(\kappa\ge2\), and \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(1\le n<d\). For \(i=1,\ldots,d\), set \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+((\kappa-1)/2)\cos\theta_i\), and \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\). Lean uses \(i\in\mathrm{Fin}\,d\) and \((i.\mathrm{val}+1/2)\pi/d\). Let \(U\sim N(0,\Lambda^{-1})\) on real Euclidean space and \(D_n=\operatorname{diag}(\cos(n\theta_i))\). The literal Gaussian constructor takes covariance \(\Lambda^{-1}\); \(\Lambda\) is precision. Its coordinate quadratic form is \(Q(x)=\sum_i\cos(n\theta_i)x_i^2\). Set \(r=(\sqrt\kappa-1)/(\sqrt\kappa+1)\), \(M=\int\|x\|^2\,d\mu\), and \(\mu_n=\int Q(x)\,d\mu\), where \(\mu=N(0,\Lambda^{-1})\). The inequalities \(0<r<1\), all denominator conditions and both integrability facts are proved internally.

lean_statement.statement:
∀ {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hnd : n < d),
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let eigenvalue : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)
  let Λ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ := Matrix.diagonal eigenvalue
  let μ : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
    multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) Λ⁻¹
  let Q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
    ∑ i : Fin d, Real.cos ((n : ℝ) * θ i) * (WithLp.ofLp x i) ^ 2
  let r : ℝ := (Real.sqrt κ - 1) / (Real.sqrt κ + 1)
  Integrable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) => ‖x‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
  Integrable Q μ ∧
  (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), ‖x‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) =
    ((d : ℝ) / Real.sqrt κ) * ((1 - r ^ (2 * d)) / (1 + r ^ (2 * d))) ∧
  (-1 : ℝ) ^ n * (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), Q x ∂μ) =
    ((d : ℝ) / Real.sqrt κ) * ((r ^ n - r ^ (2 * d - n)) / (1 + r ^ (2 * d)))

approved_definition_context: Fin d is the usual finite type with values zero through d minus one; finite sums run over all coordinates.
EuclideanSpace Real (Fin d) carries the standard Euclidean norm. WithLp.ofLp exposes its coordinate vector. Matrix.diagonal is the ordinary diagonal matrix.

ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian m S is the image of the standard Gaussian by x↦m+toEuclideanCLM(CFC.sqrt S)x. Its matrix parameter is covariance on the positive semidefinite domain; the standard totalized square root is zero outside that domain.

Matrix inverse and real inverse use standard totalized inverses. Integrable is Bochner integrability under the displayed measure; the real integral is the Bochner integral. Integrability is part of the displayed conclusion.
Natural powers, real casts, square root, cosine and pi have their standard meanings. Natural subtraction is truncated at zero, with its displayed bounds determining the relevant exponent range.

blind_reconstruction.text:
For every natural number d with d ≥ 2, every real number κ with κ ≥ 2, and every natural number n with 1 ≤ n < d, define, for each coordinate index i ∈ {0, …, d − 1},

θᵢ = (i + 1/2)π/d,
λᵢ = (κ + 1)/2 + ((κ − 1)/2) cos θᵢ.

Let Λ = diag(λ₀, …, λ_{d−1}). On the real Euclidean space Rᵈ, let μ be the centered multivariate Gaussian measure with covariance matrix Λ⁻¹. More explicitly, μ is the image of the standard Gaussian measure under the linear map whose matrix is the positive semidefinite square root of Λ⁻¹. Define the real-valued function

Q(x) = ∑_{i=0}^{d−1} cos(nθᵢ) xᵢ²

and the real number

r = (√κ − 1)/(√κ + 1).

Then x ↦ ‖x‖² and Q are both Bochner integrable with respect to μ, and their real Bochner integrals satisfy the two exact identities

∫_{Rᵈ} ‖x‖² dμ(x) = (d/√κ) (1 − r^{2d})/(1 + r^{2d}),

(−1)ⁿ ∫_{Rᵈ} Q(x) dμ(x) = (d/√κ) (rⁿ − r^{2d−n})/(1 + r^{2d}).

Here ‖·‖ is the standard Euclidean norm, all coordinate sums include every index from 0 through d − 1, and all displayed angles and scalar expressions are real. Powers have natural-number exponents. The expression 2d − n uses natural subtraction, which is ordinary nonnegative subtraction under 1 ≤ n < d. Matrix and real inverses and the real square root retain the totalized meanings in the supplied context. In this parameter range every λᵢ is positive, so Λ⁻¹ is the usual inverse and the Gaussian parameter is its ordinary positive definite covariance. The Gaussian construction agrees with the supplied totalized definition, whose matrix square root is zero outside the positive semidefinite domain; the assumptions here stay within that domain.

The assertions hold separately for every admissible triple (d, κ, n). Both integrability conclusions and both equalities concern this same μ, and Q depends on n as defined above. There is no limiting, asymptotic, approximate, almost-everywhere, or optimization assertion and no unspecified constant. All numerical factors are displayed explicitly; μ depends on d and κ, the formula for Q depends only on d and n, while its integration measure also depends on κ, and r depends only on κ.
